subject: Mutual action plan — benchmarking plan, model-variant tradeoffs, close timeline
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Delgado <sofia.delgado@starkinsights.com>, Procurement <procurement@starkinsights.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Mutual action plan: benchmarking & close timeline for Stark Insights

Hi Sofia / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the conversation today. Per Stan's ask, attached is a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) focused on the performance benchmarking you requested for your autocomplete product (512-token context, ~20-token prompt, 40 concurrent users peak). High-level asks from your side:

- Confirm acceptance criteria (latency / throughput / TTFT targets)
- Approve model variants we should include in the evaluation
- Commit to target close timeline so we can prioritize Dedicated capacity scheduling

Proposed MAP milestones and owners:
1) Benchmark design & dataset exchange — May 13 (you / us)
2) Redwood runs variant benchmarks — May 14–15 (Redwood eng: Laura + Vivek)
3) Internal review & canary config — May 16 (Redwood PM/Eng)
4) Canary + customer validation — May 18–22 (joint)
5) Procurement & contract signature — target Jun 2
6) Go-live (Dedicated capacity + rollout) — target Jun 16

Performance targets we think align with your SLA goals (please confirm):
- P95 latency (inference, end-to-end) <= 350 ms at target concurrency
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) <= 120 ms for warm requests
- Sustained throughput >= 600 tokens/sec aggregate per GPU pool (scale target)
- Concurrent sessions: support 40 active users with <10% tail degradation

Model variants we propose to include in the MAP: redwood-7b-qat, redwood-13b-8bit, redwood-70b-fp16. We will measure quality on your eval set (we discussed the 1k prompt offline) and report tradeoffs (latency vs. quality).

Can you confirm these milestones and acceptance criteria? Once you sign off, Laura and Vivek will run the bench and share results as artifacts (trace files, latency histograms, cost estimate).

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0179

From: Sofia Delgado <sofia.delgado@starkinsights.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-13T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: benchmarking & close timeline for Stark Insights

Karthik — thanks, that looks good. A few clarifications before we sign off on the MAP:

- Our primary KPI is perceived latency for end users; P95 is the right metric. We'd like P95 <= 300 ms if achievable, but can accept <= 350 ms as a backup.
- TTFT target: <= 100 ms if warm; cold startups are OK to be slower.
- Throughput: the product needs to sustain bursts up to 2000 tokens/sec across the cluster; per-GPU numbers are fine for your recommendations.
- Quality: we expect accuracy/fluency comparable to our current LLM baseline; we'll share the eval set (1k prompts) by end of day May 13.

For variants, please also include any optimized 13B/30B quantized options you recommend — if that changes the tradeoffs include them.

Procurement: our legal team prefers to close by the first week of June (target Jun 4). If you can hit that, procurement will prioritize.

Sofia
Head of Product, Stark Insights
sofia.delgado@starkinsights.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-13T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Mutual action plan: benchmarking & close timeline for Stark Insights

Laura/Vivek — forwarding Sofia's confirmation and the MAP. Key asks:

- Run the benchmark against the Stark eval (they'll upload by EOD).
- Include these variants in the run: redwood-7b-qat, redwood-13b-8bit, redwood-30b-8bit (if available), redwood-70b-fp16.
- Record: P50/P95/P99 latencies, TTFT, throughput at target concurrency (40 users / burst to 2000 tok/s), cost estimate per 1M tokens, and quality metric on their eval.

Deliverable: single ZIP of artifacts + a short CSV comparing variants. Can you turn this around by EOD May 15? I'll then consolidate and send to Sofia with a canary recommendation.

Thanks — Karthik

> On 2026-05-13 Sofia said: "Our primary KPI is perceived latency... we'll share the eval set by end of day May 13."

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-15T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Mutual action plan: benchmarking & close timeline for Stark Insights

Karthik / Vivek — ran the benchmarks using Stark's 1,024-sample eval slice. Artifacts attached: redwood_variant_compare.csv, latency_trace_20260514.zip, and a short PDF summary (stark_map_v1_results.pdf). Highlights below.

Setup notes:
- Context length: 512 tokens; avg prompt 20 tokens; eval runs on a dedicated 4xA100 cluster (profile mirrors Dedicated configuration).
- Warm runs: cache primed with a 128-prefix preload to simulate warm traffic.

Results (selected):
- redwood-7b-qat:
  - P50: 68 ms, P95: 174 ms, P99: 320 ms
  - TTFT (warm): 58 ms
  - Throughput: ~420 tokens/sec per GPU (sustained)
  - Quality (Stark eval): 85.2% recall/fluency pass rate
  - Cost estimate: low

- redwood-13b-8bit:
  - P50: 120 ms, P95: 312 ms, P99: 480 ms
  - TTFT (warm): 98 ms
  - Throughput: ~640 tokens/sec per GPU
  - Quality: 89.1%
  - Cost estimate: mid

- redwood-30b-8bit (quantized experimental):
  - P50: 230 ms, P95: 520 ms
  - TTFT: 160 ms
  - Throughput: ~340 tokens/sec per GPU
  - Quality: 91.0%
  - Notes: memory pressure higher; still experimental on our optimized kernels

- redwood-70b-fp16:
  - P50: 480 ms, P95: 780 ms, P99: 1.2 s
  - TTFT: 260 ms
  - Throughput: ~220 tokens/sec per GPU
  - Quality: 94.3%
  - Cost estimate: high

Interpretation / recommendation:
- 7B-qat gives the best latency/throughput but trails on quality (~85%). Good for non-critical prompts or latency-first features.
- 13B-8bit hits the balance: P95 ~312 ms (within Sofia's 300–350 ms acceptance window), TTFT ~98 ms, and solid quality (~89%). This is our recommended canary target for Stark to validate in production.
- 30B-8bit is promising on quality but currently has volatility in tails and higher memory/cost; recommend as a follow-up if Stark needs a quality lift after canary.
- 70B-fp16 is highest quality but cost/latency make it unsuitable for the initial rollout.

Next steps / action items:
- Karthik: share recommendation and artifacts with Sofia; propose canary timeline (May 18–22).
- Vivek: prepare canary autoscaling policy and fallback to 13B->7B variant for degradation path.
- Laura: plus attach redwood_variant_compare.csv and latency traces (attached).

Attachments: stark_map_v1_results.pdf (summary), latency_trace_20260514.zip (traces), redwood_variant_compare.csv (per-variant metrics).

Laura
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Delgado <sofia.delgado@starkinsights.com>, Procurement <procurement@starkinsights.com>

Date: 2026-05-18T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan — benchmarking plan, model-variant tradeoffs, close timeline

Sofia — quick summary and next steps based on the bench: attaching the artifacts Laura produced. TL;DR: redwood-13b-8bit is our recommended canary. It meets your P95 acceptance window (312 ms observed) and TTFT targets (~98 ms warm).

Proposed MAP adjustments & close timeline:
- Canary (13B-8bit) — May 18–22: joint validation under your traffic patterns; Redwood will provide a canary config and rollback policy. Owner: Redwood Eng (Vivek).
- Canary acceptance criteria:
  - P95 <= 350 ms under your joint test (40 concurrent users / burst patterns replicating 2k tok/s cluster-level bursts)
  - Quality >= 88% on your eval set
  - No critical errors / <0.5% error rate
- Procurement sign-off target: Jun 4 (Sofia noted legal prefers the first week of June).
- Contract execution and Dedicated capacity reservation: Jun 5–9.
- Go-live (gradual rollout): target Jun 16, with automatic fallback to 7B-qat during overloads.

If you agree, please reply with a quick "ACK" and we will schedule the canary kickoff (we plan the test window for May 19 at 10:00 AM PT).

Attachments referenced: stark_map_v1_results.pdf, latency_trace_20260514.zip, redwood_variant_compare.csv (all included in the link below).

Shared artifacts: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcDeFGhIJKl

Best — Karthik
